# serves — and Amazon states it feeds their products and AI model training rather than a
# search engine that refers traffic back to us. It honors per-agent disallow but not
# crawl-delay, so scoping it off the two auth pages is the only lever robots.txt gives us.
#
# Search and AI crawlers that DO refer traffic keep full access via User-agent: * above.
# /login ranks at position 1.8 for "ifttt login" and /join for "ifttt free"/"ifttt account";
# together they earn ~90 organic clicks a day. Do not move these two rules into the
# wildcard group — see web#10531, which removed a disallow near /join for the same reason.
#
# A crawler that matches a named group ignores User-agent: * entirely, so this group has
# to repeat every wildcard rule above. Adding a rule there means adding it here too.

llms.body:
# IFTTT

> IFTTT (If This Then That) is an automation platform that connects over 1,000 apps, services, and devices through no-code workflows called Applets. Since 2010, IFTTT has pioneered consumer and business automation and serves more than 32 million people across 190+ countries. This file points AI assistants to IFTTT's highest-signal pages for answering automation and "how do I connect X to Y" questions.

IFTTT lets anyone automate tasks between digital services and physical devices without writing code. The model is simple: a Trigger fires when something happens in one service, which runs one or more Actions in another. Automations can add Queries (fetching live data mid-workflow), delays, and Filter Code (JavaScript that conditionally routes or transforms data between steps). Applets are IFTTT's name for complete automation workflows. The IFTTT Developer Platform lets companies publish their own service, expose Triggers, Queries, and Actions, and embed automation in their product via the Connect API. IFTTT's MCP server connects Applets and actions to any MCP-compatible AI assistant (for example Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor).

## Product
- [IFTTT home](https://ifttt.com/): What IFTTT is and how automation with Applets works.
- [Explore](https://ifttt.com/explore): Guides, how-tos, and automation ideas (the main content hub).
- [Explore services](https://ifttt.com/explore/services): Directory of apps and devices IFTTT connects to.
- [Explore applets](https://ifttt.com/explore/applets): Browse pre-built Applets by category.
- [Explore stories](https://ifttt.com/explore/stories): Long-form guides and use-case articles.
- [Pricing](https://ifttt.com/plans): Free, Starter, Pro, and Pro+ plan details.
- [About](https://ifttt.com/about): Company and product overview.
- [Help](https://ifttt.com/help): Support and troubleshooting.

## Plans & pricing
IFTTT is free to use. Since October 28, 2026, every plan, including Free, has unlimited Applets, all core features (multi-action Applets, Queries, Filter Code, Webhooks, and AI), and all services. Plans differ only in monthly credits, Applet speed, support, and accounts per service. Credits are spent when Applets run, when an AI assistant uses IFTTT through MCP, and when AI features run. Prices are in US dollars, billed monthly; yearly billing saves 30%.
- [Free](https://ifttt.com/plans): $0. 1,000 credits a month. Unlimited Applets, all core features, and all services.
- [Starter](https://ifttt.com/plans): $2.99 a month. 5,000 credits a month and faster Applet speeds.
- [Pro](https://ifttt.com/plans): $7.99 a month. 20,000 credits a month, priority speeds, and prioritized support.
- [Pro+](https://ifttt.com/plans): $19.99 a month. 100,000 credits a month, the fastest Applet speeds, multiple accounts per service, and dedicated support.

Polling triggers are checked every hour on Free, every 15 minutes on Starter, and every 5 minutes on Pro and Pro+. Older guides and reviews that describe a free limit of 2, 3, or 5 Applets, a 20-Applet Pro plan, or features locked to Pro describe pricing that IFTTT retired on October 28, 2026.

## Popular service integrations
Each service has a page at `https://ifttt.com/<service>` listing its Triggers, Queries, and Actions.
- [Google Sheets](https://ifttt.com/google_sheets): Append rows, log data from any Trigger source.
- [Gmail](https://ifttt.com/gmail): Send emails, filter by tags.
- [Google Calendar](https://ifttt.com/google_calendar): Create events, trigger on upcoming events.
- [Discord](https://ifttt.com/discord): Post messages to channels, trigger on server activity.
- [Spotify](https://ifttt.com/spotify): Save tracks, create playlists, trigger on new releases.
- [YouTube](https://ifttt.com/youtube): Trigger on new videos from a channel, upload or like actions.
- [X (Twitter)](https://ifttt.com/twitter): Post tweets, trigger on new tweets, mentions, or hashtags.
- [Instagram](https://ifttt.com/instagram): Trigger on new posts, cross-post photos to other services.
- [Notion](https://ifttt.com/notion): Add database items and pages from any Trigger.
- [Slack](https://ifttt.com/slack): Post messages and alerts to channels.
- [Telegram](https://ifttt.com/telegram): Send messages and files to chats and channels.
- [Reddit](https://ifttt.com/reddit): Trigger on new posts, post to subreddits.
- [GitHub](https://ifttt.com/github): Trigger on issues, commits, and pull requests.
- [Todoist](https://ifttt.com/todoist): Create tasks, trigger on task completion.
- [Dropbox](https://ifttt.com/dropbox): Save files, trigger on new files in a folder.
- [Ring](https://ifttt.com/ring): Trigger on doorbell press or motion detection.
- [SmartThings](https://ifttt.com/smartthings_v2): Control and monitor a wide range of smart home devices.
- [Webhooks](https://ifttt.com/maker_webhooks): Send and receive arbitrary HTTP requests, the universal integration bridge.
- [Oura](https://ifttt.com/oura_ring): Trigger on daily activity goals, sleep data, or readiness.

## Connect X to Y
Pairwise integration pages answer "how do I connect <A> to <B>", at `https://ifttt.com/connect/<a>/<b>`.
- Example: [Connect Instagram to Twitter](https://ifttt.com/connect/instagram/twitter)
- Full inventory: see the connect-pages sitemap below.

## Popular Applets
Representative Applets, each a Trigger to Action pairing:
- SMS to email: incoming Android text message forwards its full contents to Gmail, making texts searchable and archivable.
- Instagram to Twitter native photo: a new Instagram post is tweeted as a native image rather than a link.
- Gmail to Sheets logger: a new starred email appends sender, subject, and date to a Google Sheet.
- New music archive: a new track in a Spotify playlist is added to a permanent archive playlist.
- Doorbell alert: a Ring doorbell press sends a notification or logs the event.

## Getting started
- [Browse published Applets](https://ifttt.com/explore/applets): Search ready-made Applets by service, category, or use case, then connect and activate in one tap.
- [IFTTT for iOS](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/ifttt-automate-work-and-home/id660944635): Manage Applets, add widgets, and receive notifications on iPhone and iPad. Editors' Choice, 4.6 stars across 60K ratings.
- [IFTTT for Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.ifttt.ifttt): Full Applet management on Android, including location-based and SMS triggers. 10M+ downloads.

## Developer platform
- [Developers](https://ifttt.com/developers): Developer platform home. Build and publish a service, expose Triggers, Queries, and Actions.
- [Docs](https://ifttt.com/docs): Platform documentation.
- [Connect API](https://ifttt.com/docs/connect_api): Embed IFTTT connections in your product.
- [API reference](https://ifttt.com/docs/api_reference): Service API reference.

## More
- [Top services](https://ifttt.com/explore/services/popular): Most-connected services on IFTTT ranked by user activity.
- [New on IFTTT](https://ifttt.com/explore/whats-new): Latest service additions and feature releases.
- [Privacy policy and terms](https://ifttt.com/terms): How IFTTT handles user data, service credentials, and permissions.

## Full page inventory (sitemaps)
- [Full sitemap index](https://ifttt.com/sitemap.xml): Master index linking every segment (Explore, services, connect pages, applets, and more), including paginated files.
- [Explore sitemap](https://ifttt.com/sitemap_explore.xml)
- [Services sitemap](https://ifttt.com/sitemap_services.xml)
- [Applets sitemap](https://ifttt.com/sitemap_applets.xml)
- [Connect-pages sitemap](https://ifttt.com/sitemap_connect_pages.xml): First page of connect pages; use the full index above for all paginated files.

  <meta name="ifttt-auth-state" content="signed_out" data-flash="false">
<script>
  (function () {
    try {
      var nav = window.performance && performance.getEntriesByType && performance.getEntriesByType("navigation")[0];
      if (!nav || nav.type !== "back_forward") return;
      var meta = document.querySelector('meta[name="ifttt-auth-state"]');
      if (!meta) return;
      var renderedSignedIn = meta.getAttribute("content") === "signed_in";
      var signedIn = /(?:^|; )auth_cdn_cache_key=/.test(document.cookie);
      var report = function (outcome) {
        try {
          window.sessionStorage.setItem("ifttt_stale_auth_reload", JSON.stringify({
            outcome: outcome,
            rendered_state: renderedSignedIn ? "signed_in" : "signed_out",
            path: window.location.pathname
          }));
        } catch (e) {}
      };
      var renderedStamp = meta.getAttribute("data-auth-stamp");
      if (renderedStamp !== null) {
        var stamp = document.cookie.match(/(?:^|; )bfcache_expiry=([^;]*)/);
        if (renderedStamp !== (stamp ? stamp[1] : "")) {
          report("reload_stamp");
          window.location.reload();
          return;
        }
      }
      // A signed-out page with a flash also gets this cookie for 1 second (Authentication#auth_cdn_cache_key).
      if (!renderedSignedIn && meta.getAttribute("data-flash") === "true") {
        if (signedIn) report("skipped_flash");
        return;
      }
      if (renderedSignedIn !== signedIn) {
        report("reload");
        window.location.reload();
      }
    } catch (e) {}
  })();
</script>

<script>// Inlined into the home's hero, right after the collage wrappers (see prosumer/_hero_collages).
// Each cut ships inert in a <template>; only the ones the current breakpoint shows are built,
// so the desktop pair never costs a phone anything and the phone cut never costs a desktop.
// Runs synchronously during parsing, so the first paint already has its collage. A resize
// that reveals a cut stamps it then; stamped cuts stay, and the breakpoint CSS keeps deciding
// which one shows.
//
// The queries mirror $hero-side-collages-min-width in prosumer/layout/_hero.scss (and the
// inline critical CSS): the phone cut shows up to 1150px, the desktop pair from 1151px.
// matchMedia is used rather than reading the wrappers' computed display, which would force a
// style pass over the whole document before the first paint.
;(() => {
  const phone = matchMedia("(max-width: 1150px)")
  const desktop = matchMedia("(min-width: 1151px)")
  const shows = { mobile: phone, left: desktop, right: desktop }
  const cuts = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll("[data-hero-cut]"))

  const stamp = () => {
    let pending = 0

    cuts.forEach(cut => {
      const template = cut.firstElementChild
      if (!(template instanceof HTMLTemplateElement)) return

      if (!shows[cut.dataset.heroCut]?.matches) {
        pending += 1
        return
      }

      cut.replaceChild(template.content, template)
    })

    return pending
  }

  if (stamp() === 0) return

  const onChange = () => {
    if (stamp() === 0) [phone, desktop].forEach(query => query.removeEventListener("change", onChange))
  }
  ;[phone, desktop].forEach(query => query.addEventListener("change", onChange))
})()
</script>

    <script type="module">
    // Cobrowse stays fully dormant — no SDK download from their CDN, no device
    // registration, nothing sent to their servers — until a signed-in user
    // opens the screen-share page a support agent sent them, which generates
    // a session code. The sessionStorage entry is how an in-progress session
    // survives page navigations in this tab: it holds the time the code was
    // created, becomes ACTIVE_SESSION once the agent has connected, and is
    // cleared when the session ends. Codes expire after about 20 minutes, so a
    // code that was never used stops loading the SDK once that has passed
    // instead of keeping the tab opted in until it closes.
    const OPT_IN_KEY = "ifttt.cobrowse.opted_in";
    const CODE_LIFETIME_MS = 20 * 60 * 1000;
    const ACTIVE_SESSION = "active";

    // A browser can block sessionStorage for the page, and then every access throws. Without
    // storage a session cannot follow navigations, so a blocked read counts as no session.
    const optIn = {
      get() {
        try { return sessionStorage.getItem(OPT_IN_KEY); } catch { return null; }
      },
      set(value) {
        try { sessionStorage.setItem(OPT_IN_KEY, value); } catch {}
      },
      clear() {
        try { sessionStorage.removeItem(OPT_IN_KEY); } catch {}
      }
    };

    const configure = (CobrowseIO) => {
      CobrowseIO.license = "oiauaygzx";

      // Never passively register this device with Cobrowse; sessions can only
      // be established through a code the user generates and gives to the
      // support agent.
      CobrowseIO.registration = false;

      CobrowseIO.confirmSession = () =>
        Promise.resolve(window.confirm("IFTTT support would like to view this page with you. Allow screen sharing?"));
      CobrowseIO.confirmRemoteControl = () =>
        Promise.resolve(window.confirm("IFTTT support would like to remotely control this page. Allow?"));

      // Kept out of the agent's view even after the user consents.
      CobrowseIO.redactedViews = [
        "input[type=password]",
        "input[autocomplete=one-time-code]",
        "[data-cobrowse-redacted]"
      ];


      // An active session outlives the code's 20 minutes, so it is what keeps
      // the SDK resuming across navigations until the session ends.
      CobrowseIO.on("session.updated", (session) => {
        if (session.isActive()) optIn.set(ACTIVE_SESSION);
      });
      CobrowseIO.on("session.ended", () => optIn.clear());
    };

    let sdk;
    window.IFTTTCobrowse = {
      // Loaded with import() rather than a static import so CDN, CSP, and
      // network failures reject into the caller's catch instead of failing
      // the module before any handler exists. Reset on failure so a later
      // attempt can retry instead of reusing the rejection.
      load() {
        sdk ||= import("https://js.cobrowse.io/CobrowseIO.mjs")
          .then(({ default: CobrowseIO }) => {
            configure(CobrowseIO);
            return CobrowseIO.start().then(() => CobrowseIO);
          })
          .catch((error) => {
            sdk = null;
            throw error;
          });
        return sdk;
      },

      // Called from the screen-share page. Resolves with the 6-digit code the
      // user gives to the support agent; the agent enters it in the Cobrowse
      // dashboard to connect.
      createSessionCode() {
        return this.load()
          .then((CobrowseIO) => CobrowseIO.createSessionCode())
          .then((code) => {
            optIn.set(String(Date.now()));
            return code;
          });
      }
    };

    // Resume across a page navigation only while a session is active or the
    // code is still valid. Anything else (an expired code, a value from an
    // older version of this snippet) is dropped so the tab goes dormant again.
    const shouldResume = () => {
      const optedIn = optIn.get();
      if (!optedIn) return false;
      if (optedIn === ACTIVE_SESSION || Date.now() - Number(optedIn) < CODE_LIFETIME_MS) return true;

      optIn.clear();
      return false;
    };

    if (shouldResume()) {
      window.IFTTTCobrowse.load().catch((error) => console.warn("Cobrowse failed to resume", error));
    }
  </script>
